svg.title: Amazon Cognito
svg.desc: Amazon Cognito. Sign-up and sign-in for your app's users: user pools issue OpenID Connect tokens, identity pools trade them for AWS credentials. Step 1, Where it sits: Cognito signs customers in and issues tokens; APIs trust them; an identity pool hands out AWS keys. Step 2, Sign in with managed login: Email, password, TOTP on managed login; a trigger adds tier: gold; code + verifier → three tokens. Step 3, Using the tokens: The authorizer checks signature, exp and scope; the identity pool trades the ID token for AWS keys. Step 4, Limits and lock-in: Revoking won't recall a JWT; mind RPS quotas, the price per active user, styling limits and lock-in.

g.text: Cognito signs customers in and issues tokens; APIs trust them; an identity pool hands out AWS keys.
Email, password, TOTP on managed login; a trigger adds tier: gold; code + verifier → three tokens.
The authorizer checks signature, exp and scope; the identity pool trades the ID token for AWS keys.
Revoking won't recall a JWT; mind RPS quotas, the price per active user, styling limits and lock-in.
all pools in a Region share
In: the migrate user trigger, or a CSV import (with password hashes on eligible pools).
Out: no API returns password hashes, so users reset or migrate as they sign in.
Regional: a multi-Region replica (add-on) signs users in, but no sign-up or TOTP.
CUSTOMER IDENTITY FOR AN APP ON AWS
The user pool is the customers' directory and an OpenID Connect provider: sign-up and sign-in pages, MFA, Sign in with Google, Lambda
triggers. API Gateway and AppSync accept its tokens, and an ALB can run its sign-in for a web app. The identity pool trades a signed-in
customer's ID token for temporary AWS credentials in an IAM role, for calls straight to AWS such as photo uploads to S3. It costs nothing.
auth.shop.example serves Cognito's sign-in pages (Essentials plan).
MFA is required: a TOTP code, or a passkey with user verification.
With Continue with Google, Google signs her in and handles MFA.
shop-web has no secret, so the code only works with its code_verifier
(S256). /oauth2/token returns an ID and an access token, 1 h each by
default (5 min to 1 day), and a refresh token, 30 days by default.
COGNITO_USER_POOLS accepts tokens the pool signed that haven't expired.
With a method scope set, it wants an access token holding orders/read,
else 401. The claims, tier included, are handed to the backend.
IDENTITY POOL: ID TOKEN IN, AWS KEYS OUT
GetId gives Ana the identity ID us-east-1:9f3c…, and the enhanced flow's
GetCredentialsForIdentity assumes photo-uploader through STS: keys for
1 hour that may only PutObject under photos-prod/u/<identity ID>/.
REVOKING DOESN'T RECALL AN ACCESS TOKEN
RevokeToken or /oauth2/revoke ends a refresh token, and Cognito's own
APIs refuse its access tokens. An API that verifies JWTs by itself still
accepts them until exp, so keep access tokens short-lived.
STYLED PAGES, AND WHEN TO PICK SOMETHING ELSE
Managed login takes a logo, colours and layout, not your own text.
Keycloak, self-hosted, gives full control of pages, flows and data;
Auth0 and Microsoft Entra External ID are the SaaS alternatives.
PutObject, signed with the AWS keys
